title: Print Layout | Tape Measure & Nesting Improvements | Clo 2026.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to print layout in CLO 2026.0 allows you to:
- Automatically calculate fabric consumption and average cost per garment based on nesting results. Additionally, ensure consistent garment appearance and prevent shading by controlling pattern direction for individual garment bundles.
- Measure the distance between any two points across patterns, fabrics, and graphics within Print Layout mode. 

01:14 - Bundle One Direction
05:21 - Tape Measure

markdown_content: ## Print Layout Access in CLO (Simulation → Print Layout) This section explains how to open the **Print Layout** workspace inside **CLO** by navigating from the **Simulation** area. It also identifies where the relevant tools appear once you switch into Print Layout mode. 1. Open your garment in **CLO**. 2. Go to the top navigation near **Simulation**. 3. Select **Print Layout** to switch views. 4. In **Print Layout**, use the tool panel on the right (including **Settings**) to control layout and simulation behavior. --- ## Settings Update: Bundle Direction Tied to Grain Direction This section covers the **Settings** update where **Bundle Direction** behavior depends on **Grain Direction**. It explains how to switch between one-way and two-way fabric layouts and how to apply grain settings per pattern piece or across colorways. ### Grain Direction and Bundle Direction behavior - If **Grain Direction** is set to **one-way**, the **Bundle One Direction** option becomes **deactivated**. - To enable bundling behavior, set **Grain Direction** to **two-way**. ### Ways to set Grain Direction to two-way You can choose **two-way** in multiple places: 1. Use the **drop-down** in the **Settings** area to set the fabric to **two-way**. 2. In **Simulation**, select **pattern pieces**, then in the **Property Editor** under **Fabric**: - Set **Grain Direction** / **Grain Orientation** - Choose **per pattern piece**. 3. Optionally **link all colorways** so grain line behavior follows the same two-way approach across colorways. ### What “Bundle One Direction” does When **Grain Direction** is **two-way**, enabling **Bundle One Direction**: - Takes **one garment** and ensures it is bundled in the **same laying direction**. - Prevents pieces within that garment (e.g., sleeves) from being laid in inconsistent directions (e.g., some sleeves flipping to another direction). --- ## Nesting Results: “Nest All Patterns” with One-Garment Bundling This section shows the practical effect of enabling/disabling **Bundle One Direction** when running **nesting**. It also clarifies how grain line orientation affects sleeves versus fronts (including a sleeve grain line of **270** vs **0**). ### Nesting workflow 1. Open **Print Layout** and go to **Settings**. 2. Enable **Bundle One Direction** as desired. 3. Click **Nest All Patterns** (or nest current fabric): - Use **Nest current fabric** when you only want to nest the currently selected material. ### Observed layout differences With **Bundle One Direction ON**: - The layout becomes less ambiguous and more cohesive per garment. - Example behavior: - **Front pieces** face the same direction relative to the garment bundle. - **Back pieces** align to match the front direction. - **Sleeves** are laid to match the garment’s bundle direction as well. With **Bundle One Direction OFF**: - The layout becomes “less complicated,” but the garment pieces may no longer maintain the same-direction bundling behavior. - Fronts and sleeves may not all share the same facing direction. ### Grain line clarification (sleeves) - The **sleeve grain line** is **270** instead of **0**, which explains why sleeves appear oriented differently while still being correct for the underlying grain setup. --- ## Tape Measure Tool in Print Layout (Distance Between Pattern Pieces) This section describes how to use the new **tape measure** tool in **Print Layout** to quickly measure spacing and distances between pattern pieces. It includes the interaction pattern (click/shift/double click) used to start and end measurements. ### How to measure 1. In **Print Layout**, locate and select the **tape measure** tool. 2. Click to start a measurement. 3. Use **Shift** to view measurement details interactively. 4. Use a **straight line** measurement workflow: - **Click once** to place the first point. - **Hold Shift** to preview or adjust. - **Double click** to end the measurement. 5. Repeat to measure spacing between specific pattern pieces (e.g., how far apart two pieces are). ### Removing measurements - Select the **state measure** option (or the measurement tool state) to make the tape measure overlay disappear. --- ## Production BOM: Cost Per Garment (Bill of Materials) This section explains how to view **cost per garment** in the **Production** area using the **BOM (Bill of Materials)**. It highlights that the view can report cost per garment rather than only totals per colorway. ### BOM cost breakdown 1. Go to **Production** in the top toolbar. 2. Open **BOM (Bill of Materials)**. 3. The BOM displays **cost per garment**—not just the total cost for a selected colorway. ### Colorway and graded-size considerations - In the demonstrated case, only **one garment** is used and there are **no graded sizes**, so the **total cost** reflects that single configuration. - If there are **graded sizes** or multiple size variations, the BOM can be used to understand how costs change across those graded components. - You can select a **color** from the **colorway** selection option to focus the cost view. ---
